([users.cs.utah.edu/~thermans/papers/vanhoof-ichr2015-in-hand-learning.pdf](https://users.cs.utah.edu/~thermans/papers/vanhoof-ichr2015-in-hand-learning.pdf)) reach a similar conclusion from a different starting point.
([elib.dlr.de/190608/1/IROS22_LearningTactileEstimator.pdf](https://elib.dlr.de/190608/1/IROS22_LearningTactileEstimator.pdf)) have formalized the state-estimation problem in this setting.

([matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf](https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf)) provide the canonical demonstration of this paradigm.

DexArt ([cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2023/poster/22341](https://cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2023/poster/22341)) extends the RL paradigm to a more demanding class of objects: articulated items such as frying pans, laptops, and boxes.
([arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877)) introduce DexMV, a pipeline that learns dexterous manipulation *from human videos* rather than from robot teleoperation.

The DexYCB benchmark ([dex-ycb.github.io](https://dex-ycb.github.io/)) provides a large-scale dataset of human grasps captured with a multi-view camera rig, together with ground-truth 6D object poses and 3D hand poses.

The Hybrid Imitation Learning (HIL) framework ([mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409](https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409)) combines behavior cloning (BC) with state cloning (SC) in a unified objective.

The tactile-modeling community has shown that rich manipulation behavior can be obtained from purely local observations when an explicit observation model is available ([roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf](https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf); [elib.dlr.de/190608/1/IROS22_LearningTactileEstimator.pdf](https://elib.dlr.de/190608/1/IROS22_LearningTactileEstimator.pdf)).

Vision-based RL, by contrast, typically delegates pose estimation to an external motion-capture system ([matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf](https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf)).

Imitation learning straddles the two: when demonstrations are extracted from human videos, the pose estimator must run on in-the-wild footage, and the quality of the learned imitation policy is tightly coupled to the quality of the extracted 3D hand and object poses ([arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877); [dex-ycb.github.io](https://dex-ycb.github.io/)).

Model-driven approaches construct an explicit transition model—either from first principles or from data—and condition the policy on its predictions ([users.cs.utah.edu/~thermans/papers/vanhoof-ichr2015-in-hand-learning.pdf](https://users.cs.utah.edu/~thermans/papers/vanhoof-ichr2015-in-hand-learning.pdf)).

Model-free RL avoids an explicit transition model but pays for it with extreme sample complexity, only achieving transfer thanks to large-scale simulation and domain randomization ([matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf](https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf); [cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2023/poster/22341](https://cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2023/poster/22341)).

Imitation learning sidesteps dynamics modeling by treating the demonstrator as an implicit model; the price is brittleness when the learner drifts off the demonstration manifold, which the HIL framework addresses by augmenting BC with a state-distribution-matching term ([mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409](https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409)).

RL discovers policies from scratch and benefits from external reward shaping, but inherits the exploration difficulties of high-dimensional, contact-rich action spaces ([matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf](https://matthiasplappert.com/publications/2020_OpenAI_Dexterous-Manipulation_IJRR.pdf); [cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2023/poster/22341](https://cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2023/poster/22341)).

Imitation learning replaces exploration with supervised signals from demonstrations, but its success hinges on the alignment between demonstrator and learner embodiment and on algorithmic devices that prevent error accumulation ([arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05877); [mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409](https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/10/3409)).

Model-driven learning typically produces a relatively simple policy around a richer model, trading policy complexity for representational complexity ([roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf](https://www.roboticsproceedings.org/rss20/p135.pdf); [elib.dlr.de/190608/1/IROS22_LearningTactileEstimator.pdf](https://elib.dlr.de/190608/1/IROS22_LearningTactileEstimator.pdf)).
